g.text: Did anyone try to stop CloudTrail logging, and did it work?
SELECT eventtime, eventname, eventsource, awsregion, sourceipaddress, useragent, errorcode, errormessag…
SELECT eventtime, eventname, eventsource, awsregion, sourceipaddress, useragent, errorcode, readonly FR…
MITRE ATT&CK impair defenses disable or modify cloud logging StopLogging DeleteTrail
in us-west-2 through the console, from IP
228.139.46.252. The call returned no error, so it worked. Before the delete, the same IP logged in at
15:47:30 and ran about 40 read-only checks (DescribeTrails, LookupEvents, GetTrailStatus,
GetEventSelectors) across all regions. That pattern looks like an attacker confirming logging was active
2019-06-07: StopLogging and StartLogging by Level6 from IP 2.251.2.5, using a Kali Linux aws-cli.
Caveats: my second query hit its 100-row limit, so I could not see all activity after the delete. I also
did not check whether a replacement trail was created. The trail is gone from the logs, so any activity
after the deletion is unlogged in that trail. This matches MITRE ATT&CK T1685.002, Disable or Modify Cloud
Log (dataset knowledge base). Treat the root session and IP 228.139.46.252 as a priority for
